planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sharply drained, slightly acidic, low-phosphorus, gravelly soil in full sun; a true Mediterranean-climate fynbos specialist that fails in clay or humid summers.

directions: Plant in sharply drained, slightly acidic, gravelly soil low in phosphorus, in full sun; oleander-leaf protea bears large, velvety flowerheads in pink and cream shades from autumn through winter on an evergreen shrub reaching 6-10 feet. Like all Proteas it is a true Mediterranean-climate specialist, thriving in coastal California-type climates but struggling in humid-summer or clay-soil regions. Never fertilize with standard phosphorus-containing feeds, which are toxic to this genus; use only compost or specialty low-phosphorus protea fertilizer if feeding at all.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sharply drained, slightly acidic, low-phosphorus soil in full sun; Compacta Protea tolerates light frost and coastal salt spray better than many Protea species.

directions: Plant in sharply drained, slightly acidic soil low in phosphorus, in full sun; Compacta Protea produces dense, pink flowerheads from winter into spring on a sturdy shrub more tolerant of light frost and coastal salt spray than many of its genus relatives. It remains a true Mediterranean-climate specialist, best suited to coastal California-type gardens rather than humid or continental climates. Avoid standard phosphorus fertilizers, which are toxic to this genus; feed only with compost or a specialty low-phosphorus protea formula.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sharply drained, slightly acidic, low-phosphorus soil in full sun; Protea eximia is regarded as one of the easier Proteas for a home grower to succeed with.

directions: Plant in sharply drained, slightly acidic soil low in phosphorus, in full sun; Protea eximia is considered one of the more forgiving Protea species for home gardeners, bearing large pink bracts in winter. It still demands the genus's characteristic sharp drainage and phosphorus-free feeding regime, but shows somewhat better tolerance of general garden conditions than the more exacting fynbos specialists. Grow it as a dramatic focal shrub in a Mediterranean-climate garden bed with excellent air circulation.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sharply drained soil in full sun; Silver Tree is short-lived (15-20 years) and intolerant of humidity or wet feet, a true Cape-climate-only specialist.

directions: Plant in sharply drained soil in full sun; Silver Tree is the iconic Table Mountain endemic, prized for its silky, silver-sheened foliage that shimmers in wind and sun, growing into a substantial tree 25-40 feet tall. It is naturally short-lived, typically 15-20 years, and demands a true Mediterranean coastal climate, failing outright in humid or wet-footed conditions. This is not a plant for the Gulf Coast or any humid-summer region; it is included here strictly for growers in coastal California-type climates.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sharply drained soil in full sun; Golden Conebush is drought-tolerant once established and popular as both a landscape shrub and cut flower.

directions: Plant in sharply drained soil in full sun; Golden Conebush produces bright yellow bracts surrounding its inconspicuous true flowers in winter, popular both as a landscape shrub and a cut-flower crop. It is drought-tolerant once established and, like other Leucadendron species, should never receive standard phosphorus fertilizer, which is toxic to the genus; feed only with compost if feeding at all. It is a Mediterranean-climate specialist best suited to coastal California-type gardens rather than humid or continental regions.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sharply drained soil in full sun; Rocket Pincushion is a strict no-phosphorus, sharp-drainage fynbos specialist unsuited to humid climates.

directions: Plant in sharply drained soil in full sun; Rocket Pincushion is a grey-leaved shrub reaching 8-12 feet, bearing striking red-and-yellow 'rocket' flowerheads from winter into spring. It is a classic fynbos-only species that demands strictly no-phosphorus feeding and sharp drainage, performing best in Mediterranean or coastal California-type climates and poorly in humid-summer regions like the Gulf Coast. Grow it as a dramatic architectural specimen in a dedicated fynbos or xeriscape bed where its exacting needs can be met.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sandy, acidic (pH 5-6.5) soil in full sun; this true Cape heath is distinct from the Northern Hemisphere Erica carnea/cinerea cultivars already in cultivation.

directions: Plant in sandy, acidic soil of pH 5 to 6.5 in full sun; Nine-Pin Heath is a true Cape heath from the South African fynbos, distinct from the hardy Northern Hemisphere Erica cultivars more commonly grown in American gardens. It bears tubular flowers in red, orange, or pink over an unusually long season, drawing sunbirds in its native range and hummingbirds where grown in the Americas. It is generally found through specialist nurseries rather than general garden centers, and performs best in a true Mediterranean or mild coastal climate.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained soil with ample water in full sun to part shade; Elegia capensis tolerates light frost to about -5°C in sheltered sites.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil with ample moisture in full sun to part shade; Horsetail Restio is a bamboo-like architectural restio reaching 5-8 feet, with distinctive chestnut-brown sheaths along jointed stems that give it a strong vertical, structural presence. It is one of the most widely available ornamental restios internationally and tolerates light frost to about -5°C (23°F) in sheltered sites, making it somewhat more forgiving than the true Protea-family fynbos plants. Needs consistent water paired with good drainage rather than the bone-dry conditions many other fynbos species prefer.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sharply drained, sandy soil in full sun; Featherhead is notoriously hard to propagate, so expect nursery supply to be inconsistent and worth waitlisting for.

directions: Plant in sharply drained, sandy soil in full sun; Featherhead is a soft, silvery-plumed fynbos shrub prized in the cut-flower trade for its unusual feathery texture, unlike almost anything else grown in American gardens. It is drought-tolerant and tolerates light frost once established, but is notoriously difficult to propagate, so specialist nurseries frequently run waitlists rather than keeping it in steady stock. Treat it as a genuine but patience-requiring acquisition for a dedicated fynbos or Mediterranean-climate collector's garden.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sandy loam, slightly acidic soil in full sun to part shade; this fynbos buttonbush is grown mainly for the florist trade and specialist landscape use.

directions: Plant in sandy loam, slightly acidic soil in full sun to part shade; fynbos buttonbush is a fine-textured shrub bearing round, cream-to-red button flowerheads widely used in the cut-flower trade. It is a genuine garden plant but retail live-plant supply is patchier in the United States than in Australia or New Zealand, where it is more commonly stocked by retail nurseries. Give it the same Mediterranean-climate, sharp-drainage conditions as other fynbos shrubs, and expect to source it through a specialty supplier rather than a general garden center.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sharply drained, sandy soil in full sun; Silver Brunia is primarily grown commercially for the cut-flower and wholesale florist trade, with limited live-plant retail outside South Africa and New Zealand.

directions: Plant in sharply drained, sandy soil in full sun; Silver Brunia is a Western Cape fynbos endemic bearing small, silver-foliaged button flowers, grown primarily for the wholesale cut-flower and florist trade rather than as a mainstream potted garden plant. Live-plant retail availability is limited outside South Africa and New Zealand, so sourcing it for a home garden requires a specialty fynbos or protea-family nursery. Give it the same Mediterranean-climate, phosphorus-free, sharply drained conditions required by other fynbos genera.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun; Dekriet is drought-tolerant once established and hardy to about 20°F, more cold-tolerant than most true fynbos shrubs.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; Dekriet is an architectural restio-grass reaching 4-6 feet, with golden-brown summer flower spikes on female plants, traditionally harvested in South Africa for thatching. It is drought-tolerant once established and hardy to about 20°F, notably more cold-tolerant than the true Protea-family fynbos shrubs, making it a somewhat easier entry point into restio gardening. Supply from US specialty nurseries can be real but intermittent, since at least one carrying nursery periodically runs out of production stock.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun; White Diosma is one of the most widely and reliably stocked fynbos shrubs, suited to general garden center availability.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; White Diosma is a fine-textured, aromatic-foliage Cape fynbos shrub covered in masses of tiny white star-shaped flowers, complementing the pink-flowered Coleonema pulchellum already in cultivation. It is widely and reliably stocked, more mainstream than most other fynbos genera, making it a practical entry point for gardeners wanting fynbos character without hunting down a specialty supplier. It is drought-tolerant once established and benefits from a light post-bloom trim to keep its fine, feathery texture dense.
